## About BlueBench


BlueBench measures how well AI models do real defensive security work. The suite contains 74 tasks evaluated in a common harness, with task-specific prompts and tools over the raw telemetry. Six benchmarks in two series feed four tracks: incident response, threat hunting, detection engineering, and malware analysis. Those roll up into the capability, reliability, and cost leaderboards.

### BlueBench-Intrusion


Datasets of real intrusion logs. Each benchmark is a genuine hands-on-keyboard intrusion captured in production-grade telemetry: EDR, host and cloud audit logs, Zeek network metadata, and the alerts a SOC would actually see. Nothing is synthesized.


- [Intrusion-003 AWS Cloud Intrusion 8 tasks · 16 models](https://www.cotool.ai/research/aws-cloud-intrusion)
- [Intrusion-002 Windows Enterprise Intrusion 40 tasks · 16 models](https://www.cotool.ai/research/windows-enterprise-intrusion)
- [Intrusion-001 macOS Threat Investigation 14 tasks · 16 models](https://www.cotool.ai/research/macos-threat-investigation)


### BlueBench-Simulation


Every environment is a fully generated enterprise: routine baseline activity, a simulated intrusion, and benign lookalikes that punish pattern-matching without verification. Because we author the environment, the ground truth is complete and none of the data can have leaked into training sets.


- [Simulation-003 Impact & Exfiltration 3 tasks · 16 models](https://www.cotool.ai/research/bluebench-simulation-003)
- [Simulation-002 Identity & Active Directory Attacks 4 tasks · 16 models](https://www.cotool.ai/research/bluebench-simulation-002)
- [Simulation-001 Initial Access & Command-and-Control 5 tasks · 16 models](https://www.cotool.ai/research/bluebench-simulation-001)

## Incident Response


Investigate an alert end to end and write the incident report: scope, affected hosts and accounts, attacker tradecraft, impact, and the response actions warranted. Graded against a hidden rubric.
